cards.name: Object Data
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Object Data docker (tooltip: Object Data Docker), where you attach data fields to the selected object, such as a name, cost or comment plus any custom fields you add, and read them back. It changes nothing visible on the page; the data rides along with the object in the .cdr file.
use_for: tagging parts in a technical illustration or catalogue with part numbers and prices
keeping per-object notes (supplier, material, job cost) on sign and display layouts
naming objects so a script or a later reviewer can find them
avoid: renaming or reordering objects only: the Objects docker does that directly
data-driven layouts (one card per spreadsheet row): use Print Merge, not object data
cards.how: Check item: tick to open the docker, untick to close it. Select an object, then type values into its fields; the docker's field editor adds, renames or deletes fields for the document. Disabled in Page Sorter view and full-screen preview (enable binding).
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("0de570eb-18ef-4532-9415-3ca1b3f63470") toggles the docker (docker guid 799476ff-2b80-43cb-b51a-a31ac9141618). The data itself: ActiveDocument.DataFields.Add(...) and Shape.ObjectData("<field>").Value (unverified).

cards.name: Object Styles
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Object Styles docker, CorelDRAW's style sheet: saved outline, fill, character, paragraph, frame and transparency styles (and style sets that bundle them) that you create from an object, apply to others and edit in one place, so every object using a style updates together. Colour styles live in their own Color Styles docker.
use_for: a consistent heading / body text system across a brochure or multipage catalogue
brand outline and fill settings reused on every icon in a set
restyling many objects at once by editing the style instead of each object
avoid: a one-off look on a single object: set it in the Properties docker
sharing colours that must update everywhere: use Color Styles for the colours themselves
cards.how: Check item: Ctrl+F5 opens or closes the docker. Select a styled object and create a new style or style set from it, then select other objects and apply the style; editing a style's properties in the docker updates every object linked to it.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("41607d8d-b620-ab8f-4d92-cb10b90a1402") toggles the docker (docker guid dbda185b-ac02-f6b4-4052-654348a46a39). Applying a style without the docker: Shape.Style.ApplyStyle("<style name>"); the document's styles are in ActiveDocument.StyleSheet (unverified).

cards.name: Palettes
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Palettes docker, where colour palettes are managed: open, create and organise palettes, browse the palette libraries (process and spot colour books such as Pantone), and choose which palettes appear on screen as palette bars. The same command also sits at Window > Color Palettes > Palettes.
use_for: loading a spot-colour book for print jobs that need named inks
building a client brand palette and keeping it open beside the page
hiding palettes you do not use to free up screen space
avoid: colours that must update across the design when changed: make them Color Styles instead of plain palette swatches
picking one-off colours: the Color docker or the fill/outline pickers are quicker
cards.how: Check item: tick to open the docker. Open or create a palette there, then show it as a palette bar to click-apply fill (left click) and outline (right click) colours.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("c1db12ea-8628-4768-9ced-f70f940527c9") toggles the docker (docker guid a2f385ec-72c6-4364-bead-4cd09e6dda93). Palettes from a script: Application.Palettes.Open("<file>") and Application.ActivePalette (unverified).

cards.name: Sources
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Sources docker. In 25.1 its UI binds to the links-and-anchors data source and its buttons read Open Link, Sync linked file, Break link, Refresh List, New Link, New Bookmark, Add linked file and Delete, so it lists the document's external sources (linked files and hyperlinks / bookmarks) and lets you refresh, re-sync, break or add them. The exact list columns were not probed, so treat the details as unverified.
use_for: checking which placed images are linked rather than embedded before sending a file out
re-syncing linked files after the originals were edited
adding bookmarks and hyperlinks for an interactive PDF
avoid: a file that will travel without its linked originals: break or embed the links first (or collect them for output)
web rollovers: the Links and Rollovers docker is the separate tool for those
cards.how: Check item: tick to open the docker. Pick an entry in the list, then use the buttons above it (open, sync linked file, break link, refresh list) or below it (new link, new bookmark, add linked file, delete).
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("2972bbb3-832c-4847-8efe-96b62bc78488") toggles the docker (docker guid 1a0af10a-c0c8-fead-4f94-fb89f4fc2db2). Link work without the docker: Shape.Bitmap.ExternallyLinked / Shape.Bitmap.UpdateLink for linked bitmaps, Shape.URL.Address for hyperlinks (unverified).

cards.name: Transform
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Transform docker, the numeric way to position, rotate, scale and mirror, size and skew the selection: you type exact values, pick the anchor point, and can apply the change to the original or to a number of copies.
use_for: placing an object at exact page coordinates for print layouts
radial repeats: rotating copies around a centre for badges, dials and patterns
mirroring a half-drawn symmetric logo into a copy
resizing to an exact width or height for a die line or label
avoid: rough moves and scales by eye: drag with the Pick tool or use the property bar
lining objects up with each other: Align and Distribute does that directly
cards.how: Check item: Alt+F7 opens or closes the docker. Pick a page (Position, Rotate, Scale and Mirror, Size, Skew), type the values, choose the anchor point and relative / absolute mode, set Copies (0 transforms the original), then Apply.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("4f467f4a-9350-4d98-8a9a-e077c18f7fd6") toggles the docker (docker guid 9d5d7bc9-3227-1195-4c7a-fe91788e2367). The transforms themselves: Shape.Move, Shape.Rotate / RotateEx, Shape.Stretch, Shape.SetSize, Shape.Skew, Shape.Flip, with Shape.Duplicate for copies (unverified).

cards.name: Tray
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Tray docker (new in version 23 per DrawUI.xml): a holding area of one or more named trays where you collect content to reuse later and drag it back onto the page. Its strings include Add new tray, Rename tray, Delete tray, Remove from tray and Open tray file. What content types a tray accepts in 25.1 was not probed.
use_for: gathering logos, photos and clip art for a project before laying it out
keeping reusable elements one drag away while building several layouts
avoid: assets that must update everywhere they are used: symbols or linked files are better than tray copies
a document's own pages and objects: use the Pages and Objects dockers
cards.how: Check item: tick to open the docker. Add a tray, drop content into it, then drag items from the tray onto the page; trays can be renamed, deleted or opened from a tray file.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("17714be3-7c69-4959-bed9-90b16eeaa929") toggles the docker (docker guid 83f56d75-2bdd-4fb7-91db-b38894f5684d). No object-model access to tray content is known.

cards.name: Views
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Views docker (the old View Manager): saves the current zoom level and scroll position, and optionally the page, as a named view, then jumps back to it with one click. It changes only how you look at the document, not the artwork.
use_for: jumping between detail areas of a large poster or signage file
saved close-ups for checking small print, registration or crop marks
consistent zoom positions while presenting a layout to a client
avoid: fitting everything on screen once: Zoom to Fit / Zoom to Page is quicker
comparing two areas side by side: open a New Window instead
cards.how: Check item: Ctrl+F2 opens or closes the docker. Zoom and scroll to an area, add a view and name it; click a view to return to it. Disabled when editing in place, in Page Sorter view and in full-screen preview (enable binding).
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("22cc7130-3cb1-4ee4-ad9e-3040dc963a44") toggles the docker (docker guid 18d6991b-8ef8-4b48-be1a-d55f769648a9). Saved views from a script: ActiveDocument.CreateView(Name, OriginX, OriginY, Zoom, Page) and ActiveDocument.Views(n).Activate (unverified).

cards.name: New Window
cards.summary: Opens a second window onto the active document, so you can view the same file at two zoom levels or two areas at once; edits in either window change the same document. Needs an open document (disabled with none) and is off while editing in place.
use_for: working on a small detail while watching the whole layout update in another window
comparing two pages or spreads of one document side by side
avoid: keeping a frozen copy to compare against: duplicate the page or save a copy, since both windows show live edits
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("ee06028c-8f7c-4efd-b590-91b4c50fb734") (onInvoke AppDS.OnWindowNew). Object-model alternative: ActiveWindow.NewWindow (unverified).

cards.name: Refresh Window
cards.summary: Redraws the active drawing window from scratch, clearing screen leftovers after heavy edits or a stalled redraw. It does not change the document. Needs an open document.
use_for: clearing redraw artefacts after complex effects, bitmaps or slow screen updates
checking the true screen state before taking a screenshot of the layout
avoid: expecting it to fix wrong colours or a missing effect: it only redraws what the document already holds
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("24045d4b-73aa-47cb-ba30-471bb1893be3") (onInvoke WViewCommandsDS.OnRefreshScreen). Object-model alternative: ActiveWindow.Refresh (unverified).

cards.name: Tile Horizontally
cards.summary: Arranges the open drawing windows as horizontal strips stacked one above another, each the full width of the workspace. It was disabled in every harvest probe state (enable binding UIMgr.EnableTileWindows), including with one document open, so it needs two or more document windows (a second document or a New Window).
use_for: comparing two wide layouts (banners, web headers) one above the other
copying objects between documents by dragging across stacked windows
avoid: tall portrait pages: Tile Vertically gives each window more height
a single open window: the command stays disabled
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("a52e08a7-102d-198f-41dc-8db7ef485ee0") (onInvoke UIMgr.OnTileHorizontally); no effect while it is disabled.

cards.name: Tile Vertically
cards.summary: Arranges the open drawing windows side by side as vertical columns, each the full height of the workspace. Disabled in every harvest probe state (enable binding UIMgr.EnableTileWindows), so it needs two or more document windows open.
use_for: comparing two portrait pages or poster versions side by side
dragging artwork from a reference document into the working one
avoid: wide landscape artwork: Tile Horizontally wastes less space
a single open window: the command stays disabled
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("1b2d92c5-f83a-c0bc-4eef-f9fe3706cba5") (onInvoke UIMgr.OnTileVertically); no effect while it is disabled.

cards.name: Custom
cards.summary: The Custom choice in the Default Button Size radio group for toolbar buttons. Its visible binding shows it only when the default button size is already set to Custom, so it acts as a read-out of a custom size set elsewhere rather than a way to choose one. DrawUI.xml also has a Global button size list in the customization options and a per-toolbar Size list; which of them leads to the Custom state was not probed.
use_for: seeing that a non-standard toolbar button size is in effect
avoid: trying to pick a custom size here: choose Small, Medium or Large from this menu, or use the customization options' Global button size or a toolbar's own Size list
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("1ed29b86-73ce-4c4d-8b2d-1a9322ba3de5") (radio item; normally hidden, see summary).

review.changes: summary + avoid: named the real settings found in DrawUI.xml (Global button size list, per-toolbar Size list) instead of 'where that custom size is set was not probed'

cards.name: Large
cards.summary: Sets the default size of toolbar buttons to Large (radio choice in Window > Toolbars > Default Button Size). Only the interface changes; the document is untouched.
use_for: high-resolution or touch screens where small icons are hard to hit
screen recordings and tutorials where viewers must read the toolbar
avoid: small laptop screens: large buttons push toolbars onto extra rows, use Small or Medium
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("d447478a-6adb-4e7e-a743-3d414b6a2d7e")

cards.name: Medium
cards.summary: Sets the default size of toolbar buttons to Medium (radio choice in Window > Toolbars > Default Button Size), the middle step between Small and Large. Interface only.
use_for: a balance of readable icons and screen space on a typical desktop monitor
avoid: cramped screens where every pixel of canvas counts: use Small
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("d4b11d74-e410-47ca-a36b-484b7d3de19c")

cards.name: Small
cards.summary: Sets the default size of toolbar buttons to Small (radio choice in Window > Toolbars > Default Button Size), giving the most room to the drawing window. Interface only.
use_for: maximising canvas space on a laptop or a single small monitor
avoid: high-DPI or touch screens where small buttons become hard to read and hit: use Medium or Large
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("8645ceb3-55af-47c1-9113-9809b0dbfdcd")

cards.name: Lock Toolbars
cards.summary: Toggles the lock on toolbars so they cannot be dragged, undocked or rearranged by accident; the setting is the app preference Framework/LockToolbars. Disabled during print preview.
use_for: keeping a tuned workspace layout stable on a shared or touch workstation
stopping accidental toolbar drags while working fast
avoid: while customising the layout: unlock first, arrange, then lock again
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("7b90fb1f-daba-4dc7-b03f-883516fe9f70") toggles the AppPrefMgr preference Framework/LockToolbars.

cards.name: Menu bar
cards.summary: Shows or hides CorelDRAW's menu bar (app preference Framework/MenuBarVisible). Hiding it frees a row of screen space; commands stay reachable through toolbars, dockers and shortcuts.
use_for: a minimal, keyboard-driven workspace with more room for the canvas
bringing back a menu bar that was hidden by accident or by an imported workspace
avoid: hiding it without a way back: this toggle sits in the Window menu, which disappears with the bar, so bring it back with the same command by script (InvokeItem) or by resetting the workspace
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("0e19571d-4639-4372-bbc0-0745af1d8f62") toggles the AppPrefMgr preference Framework/MenuBarVisible.

review.changes: avoid: the old line said 'this same command' restores it without noting that its own menu is hidden too

cards.name: Status bar
cards.summary: Shows or hides the status bar at the bottom of the window (app preference Framework/StatusBarVisible). Its sections in DrawUI.xml report object information and details, fill and outline colour, cursor coordinates, tool hints, the document colour profiles and background tasks.
use_for: checking an object's fill, outline and type at a glance while working
hiding it for extra canvas height during presentations or screen recordings
avoid: relying on it for exact sizes: the property bar and Transform docker show editable values
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("00ee6da6-9ca3-4362-9746-60b8f4728314") toggles the AppPrefMgr preference Framework/StatusBarVisible.

review.changes: summary: listed the status bar's real sections from DrawUI.xml (adds tool hints, colour profiles, background tasks)

cards.name: Delete
cards.summary: Deletes a user workspace permanently (the app's strings include the warning that the selected workspace will be deleted permanently). It was disabled in every harvest probe state, although the workspace manager was available (Export and Import were enabled), so DeleteWorkspaceEnabled was false with the built-in workspace active: it needs a user-created workspace to delete.
use_for: cleaning out old or test workspaces from the Workspace menu
avoid: a workspace you may want later: export it first with Window > Workspace > Export
the built-in workspaces: they cannot be deleted (the command stays disabled)
cards.how: Make or switch to a user workspace, then choose Delete. The confirmation dialog (DrawUI.xml) has no workspace list: it warns that the selected workspace will be deleted permanently and, when it applies, that the Default workspace will be set as your current workspace; click Delete to confirm or Cancel. Which workspace it removes was not probed live, but that layout points to the active one.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("d7574a40-4f6c-4029-863e-9f22e0988f35") (onInvoke CustomizationDS.OnDeleteWorkspace); disabled with a built-in workspace active and asks for confirmation. No object-model delete call is known.

review.changes: how: replaced the 'not probed whether it asks which workspace' guess with the confirmation dialog's real content from DrawUI.xml (no list, permanent-delete warning, conditional 'Default workspace will be set as current' line, Delete / Cancel)

cards.name: Export
cards.summary: Opens the Export Workspace dialog, which saves chosen parts of the current workspace (the dialog asks you to select the workspace elements to export) to a .cdws workspace file, for backup or to move a setup to another computer or user.
use_for: backing up a customised workspace before reinstalling or upgrading
rolling out one studio workspace (menus, toolbars, shortcuts) to every designer
avoid: sharing design assets such as palettes or styles: export those from their own dockers
cards.how: Tick the workspace elements to include (for example menus, toolbars, dockers, shortcut keys), choose a file name and location, and save the .cdws file.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("fc9a2b1b-b7e1-46ab-a9bc-0627e6b5c73f") opens the dialog only (onInvoke CustomizationDS.OnExportWorkspace). No object-model export call is known.

cards.name: Import
cards.summary: Opens the Import Workspace dialog, which reads a .cdws workspace file and brings in the elements you pick, either into the current workspace (the app's strings say this overwrites the current workspace with the new elements) or into a new workspace that includes them.
use_for: setting up a new machine with a studio's standard workspace
bringing in a colleague's shortcut keys or toolbars without replacing your own layout
avoid: importing straight into a tuned workspace you have not exported first: create a new workspace from the import instead
cards.how: Browse to the .cdws file, tick the workspace elements to import, then choose whether they go into the current workspace or a new one and finish.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("1f3512de-dbbe-4ca8-8284-d877bce90fd1") opens the dialog only (onInvoke CustomizationDS.OnImportWorkspace). No object-model import call is known.

review.changes: summary: the current-workspace option overwrites it (app string 'Overwrite current workspace with the new workspace elements')

cards.name: New
cards.summary: Opens the New Workspace dialog, which creates a named workspace based on an existing one (its Base on list), with an optional description and a Set as Current check box, so you can customise a copy without changing the original; it then appears in the Window > Workspace menu.
use_for: a task-specific layout (sign making, page layout, illustration) you can switch to in one click
experimenting with toolbar and docker changes while keeping the default intact
avoid: names that start with an underscore or contain \ / : * ? " < > | or a full stop: the app rejects them
cards.how: The dialog has Name, Base on, Description and Set as Current: type a name, pick the workspace to base it on, optionally describe it, tick Set as Current to switch to it at once, then OK.
cards.script_api: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("869a8eec-a00d-4c37-aa4f-1bbaf57f46a3") opens the dialog only (onInvoke CustomizationDS.OnNewWorkspace). No object-model create call is known.

review.changes: summary + how: the dialog's fields read from DrawUI.xml (Name, Base on, Description, Set as Current via NewWorkspaceDS); removed the wrong 'whether it switches to it at once was not probed', since Set as Current controls that; confidence medium -> high
